known_issues.summary: The 2026 frontier open-weight releases do not fit on the evaluation hardware, so the model set is bounded by serving capacity rather than by selection.
known_issues.detail: Checked 2026-08-12. Each evaluation host has 4 x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell at 96 GB, 384 GB total, and there is no fast interconnect between the two hosts, so tensor parallelism does not cross machines. Qwen3.8 shipped that day as a single configuration, Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B: 4,892 GB in bf16 and 2,496 GB in the official FP8 release, 6.5x the total VRAM of one host. There is no official 27B - Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B returns 401, and the Qwen3.8-27B repositories on the Hub are third-party derivatives, so publishing one under the Qwen3.8 name would misattribute it. moonshotai/Kimi-K3, open-weight since 2026-07-27, is 1,561 GB, 4x one host. The largest configuration on the leaderboard is deepseek_v4_flash at 149 GB. The largest addition that would run at a precision comparable to the existing rows is Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 at 127 GB, and it was declined because Qwen3.5 predates the Qwen3.6-27B already published, so it adds a scale point while reading as a newer model. This is a statement about the benchmark's reach, not a gap to be closed quietly: a reader comparing this leaderboard to a hosted-API benchmark should know the ceiling is 149 GB of weights.

known_issues.summary: The published ministral_3_14b_reasoning_2512 rows are a NON-reasoning run of the reasoning checkpoint. The scores are real; the reasoning label is not.
known_issues.detail: Both published runs produced zero reasoning traces - task1 0/184 at a mean of 723 output tokens, task2 0/4844 at a mean of 80 - while their run_config.json files claim parameter_profile reasoning_v2_temp0_6_top_p1_max8192 and response_mode reasoning_final. The reasoning arm's outputs are SHORTER than the instruct sibling's (1,011 and 114). Cause: Mistral has no thinking switch. The [THINK] instruction lives in the chat template's default_system_message, injected only when the request carries no system turn (messages[0]['role'] != 'system'). Every request here sends the task prompt as a system turn, so the task prompt replaced the instruction that makes the model think. No server flag reaches it: --default-chat-template-kwargs has no such variable in this template and --reasoning-parser mistral has no [THINK] block to separate. This is a second, independent mechanism from the enable_thinking variable used by the Gemma and Qwen arms, and a startup gate written against enable_thinking passes this run silently. It survived four days on the board because nothing in the artifacts records the server flag that actually decides. Detection is now scripts/evaluation/generation/assert_reasoning_trace.py, which reads the artifact rather than the flag and checks both directions. RESOLUTION: the row was REMOVED from active.models on 2026-08-12 rather than regenerated. A prompt variant carrying the vendor's own [THINK] block verbatim was built and measured first; it restored the table and the conclusion (7/8 to 8/8 on both) but only 3-4 of 8 responses actually produced a trace, against the 95% the artifact assertion requires, and prefilling the marker into the assistant turn did not raise it. Removing a system turn so the template can inject its own instruction did not produce a trace either, so no serving-side mechanism reached this model. The published numbers stand as a NON-reasoning run of the reasoning checkpoint and are retained under runs/ for provenance; the board simply no longer claims a Mistral reasoning configuration. The four prompt variant files were deleted with the row.

known_issues.summary: Every published judge batch records `structured_output_whitespace: "disabled"` in its run config, and no judge server ever ran that way. The field is written by the client from its own --structured-output-whitespace flag, which is a DECLARATION about how the server was started and is never sent on the wire; serve_judge.sh set no structured-output backend option at all, so every batch was decoded under xgrammar's permissive JSON grammar.
known_issues.detail: Discovered 2026-08-14 by an abandoned Task 1 rubric v15 re-judge. 1,000 of its 3,075 responses stopped exactly at the 1,200-token cap having emitted `{"conclusion_alignment":` and then roughly 1,190 tokens of `\n  ` - all 1,000 collapse to that one whitespace-stripped prefix, so it is a greedy degenerate loop, not a judge writing at length. The permissive grammar puts a `[ \n\t]*` Kleene star between every pair of JSON tokens; at temperature 0 a whitespace token that wins once reinforces itself and nothing bounds it. Raising the output budget buys more whitespace, not more judgement. PUBLISHED NUMBERS ARE UNAFFECTED: the longest v14 completion across 3,906 scored Task 1 responses is 191 tokens, so no published batch came near the cap and none shows the loop. The exposure was always there and was never taken. FIX: serve_judge.sh now passes --structured-outputs-config '{"backend":"xgrammar","disable_any_whitespace":true}' - the backend must be named, because the option is rejected under backend=auto, which is the likely reason it was dropped when that file was written - and refuses to report ready until a probe request comes back with the whitespace pinned. READ THE GUARD BEFORE CHANGING IT: `any_whitespace=False` does not forbid whitespace, it forbids ARBITRARY whitespace, by pinning the separators to json.dumps' defaults `", "` and `": "`, each carrying one space. A guard that rejects any whitespace fires on a healthy server; this one re-serialises the probe with those separators and requires the bytes back, and asks for indentation so a permissive server is caught rather than merely observed. ARTIFACT REMOVED 2026-08-15: the abandoned v15 batch that exposed this (model_evaluation/discarded/all17_task1_judge_v15_20260814_DISCARDED_whitespace_loop, 33 MB) was deleted in the same cleanup that reclaimed the judge batch files. The measurements above - 1,000 of 3,075 responses stopping at the 1,200-token cap, all collapsing to the one whitespace-stripped prefix, against a longest v14 completion of 191 tokens over 3,906 scored responses - are the record. No published number ever depended on that directory.
known_issues.consequence: Judging from 2026-08-14 runs under a pinned-separator grammar and the published batches did not. The difference is formatting whitespace inside a JSON object whose values the rubric reads, so scores are comparable; a new arm judged under v14 today can still be placed beside the 13 published rows. What changed is that the loop is now impossible rather than merely improbable.
known_issues.evidence: model_evaluation/judge/all17_task1_judge_v15_20260814 (the abandoned batch, kept as the evidence); metrics_binding_20260813/serve_judge.sh

known_issues.summary: The v4 Task 2 judge summary carries an empty execution block because the run was sharded.
known_issues.detail: Recorded 2026-08-15. The batch was judged in seven shards. The summariser verifies that a run config's batch_sha256 equals the build config's, and a shard's run config necessarily declares its own shard's hash, so --task2-run-config could not be passed and `execution` came out as {}. The scores are unaffected and were independently checked here: the 127 GB task2.batch.jsonl hashes to d5c59ecbe86c6de048d4ddd65ff8ea8dc9fd285885b5df1b865c60560910edfa, matching the build config exactly; all 62,938 dispatched custom_ids appear in the output with none missing, none extra and none duplicated, the 34 remaining manifest records being candidate format failures that carry a null custom_id and were never dispatched; and all seven shard run configs declare the same judge identity, qwen3_6_27b / Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B / 6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9. What is missing is the recorded execution provenance, not the correctness of the numbers. A future sharded batch should merge the shard configs into one execution record rather than dropping the flag.

known_issues.summary: Every multimodal Task 2 run reports 4,844 input_hash_mismatches and structurally_complete false. Nothing is wrong with them; the check does not apply.
known_issues.detail: Found 2026-08-15 while asking why the site said 26 of 32 runs were structurally audited. The validator compares each response's input_sha256 against the SOURCE manifest's input_sha256. A multimodal manifest is derived from that source and deliberately carries the source's input_sha256 through in its metadata - that pass-through is what lets a derived record still reconcile against the manifest record and registry entry it claims - while the runner records the hash of the multimodal messages it actually sent. Two different quantities, so the comparison fails on every record: 4,844 of 4,844 on each of the six multimodal arms, and 0 of 4,844 on all nine caption-only arms. Condition predicts the outcome perfectly, which is the signature of a scope error rather than of corruption. THE COMPARISON THAT APPLIES: input_sha256 == the run's own manifest's messages_sha256. Run across all six arms on 2026-08-15 - 29,064 records, zero mismatches, zero unmatched ids - so the multimodal runs are verified, just not by the field that was being read. The site no longer counts input_hash_mismatches toward integrity when the run's condition is multimodal, and reports 32 of 32. The frozen validation reports are left alone under the immutability policy. OWED: the validator itself should compare against the manifest the run actually used rather than the source it was derived from, so a future multimodal run does not ship a report that reads as broken.

GEMMA4 EMITS NO THINKING MARKER, so a grep for <think> can never detect this: with no reasoning parser attached the model emits a bare 'thought' line. The sound check is the token budget - about 1300 with final_response_extraction provider_separated_reasoning is correct, about 400 means thinking was off. final:true and errors:0 hold under both failures and cannot be used.

The other six reasoning-track arms carry their own boundary and were unaffected: the two DeepSeek arms are API and return provider_separated_reasoning, huatuogpt_3_32b_reasoning / nemotron_3_5_lightning_reasoning / qwen3_8_27b_reasoning emit their own closed <think> and land on closed_think_suffix, and medreason_8b lands on markdown_final_answer. gemma4 is the only arm whose boundary comes entirely from outside, so it is the only one the missing flags could expose.

task1.note: INPUT MODALITY: multimodal. The case is presented with slides, and the benchmark's input is the case summary, the slide images and their captions - each marker replaced by its image with that slide's caption left immediately after it, so the two arrive bound together. Every vision-capable configuration publishes a multimodal run and results_catalog.json records `condition` per run, so a caption-only row is never silently used to fill a multimodal gap. Text-only models can only take the caption-only condition, so they are labelled ablation_caption_only and the sound comparison remains each vision-capable model against its own caption-only score rather than across the two conditions. OUTPUT CONTRACT: transcript, adopted 2026-08-30. A response is one <discussion> block of `<turn N> [role]: ...` lines followed by one <conclusion> block, from tumor_board_simulation_multimodal_v3 (vision) and tumor_board_simulation_transcript_captiononly_v1 (text-only). It replaces the TABLE contract published from 2026-08-19 - `| Role | Response |` rows plus a `Conclusion:` line, from multimodal_v2 / captiononly_v4 - whose runs are filed under classified_nonactive.superseded_task1_table_contract_20260830 and named per row in `superseded_table_contract_path`. The swap is the largest single move the board has taken: Spearman 0.855 with 14 of 17 rows changing place, against 0.985 for the v25 -> v31 rubric swap, so how the room is asked to speak moves the ranking further than how the conclusion is graded. `condition` is unchanged for all 17 rows - the same seven models stay multimodal and the same ten ablation_caption_only - so the contract is the only thing that varies. The judge rubric, the judge model and the images the judge sees are also unchanged, and the four metric sources were re-run together on the new runs: no metric on the board reads a table-contract number. All three - conclusion_alignment, ROUGE-L and BERTScore - score the same 3,114 conclusions with the same 14 candidate_format_failures, and ROUGE-L verifies byte-for-byte that its candidate is the string the judge scored. Task 1 is scored over the 184 test cases of video_split_60_10_30_v3 on the de-leaked manifest after the cross-site fixes and the two re-anchored cases. The runs are natively 184 - the manifest holds 184 records and generation drew 184 - and run_expected_records audits the same 184. The published rubric is task1_judge_v31, adopted 2026-08-30 in place of v25, which had replaced v22 on 2026-08-22. v31 compresses v22/v25's fifteen-line Differences list to four lines and drops the five difference flags v25 added, leaving conclusion_alignment as the only output. It scores every arm LOWER - all 17 fall, mean -0.146 - while leaving the ordering almost intact: Spearman 0.985 against v25, six rows moving one or two places and none crossing the top five. So v31 numbers are not comparable to v25 or v22 ones in level, but a rank read off either board is close to the same board. What follows describes the v22 change and is kept because it is the reason the judge is shown the slides at all.  It scores the extracted Conclusion alone on one dimension, conclusion_alignment, and keeps major_error as a secondary flag. Two things changed together and both move scores down, so v22 numbers are not comparable to the v14 ones they replace: the judge is now SHOWN the slides as images rather than told about them in captions, so it and a vision candidate look at the same evidence; and the 1-5 anchors were rewritten, which shifts mass toward the lower bands - pooled over all 17 arms the distribution went 18.0/33.2/33.0/15.4/0.4 percent under v14 to 16.8/51.1/21.9/9.9/0.3 under v22. Every arm fell, by 0.10 to 0.37, and the ordering moved: Spearman between the two boards is 0.865. A response with no extractable conclusion is a candidate_format_failure and is scored at the rubric's own floor of 1, the anchor for stating no management recommendation at all, so the leaderboard mean covers all 184 cases for every model. It is reported from dimensions_all_responses; dimensions keeps the mean over answered cases only, so the measurement and this reporting rule stay separable. On 2026-08-11 two active configurations were affected - ministral_3_14b_instruct_2512 51 and medreason_8b 43 - and all 94 have finish_reason=stop with a median 829-1046 output tokens against a 4,096 or 8,192 cap, so they stopped of their own accord with headroom to spare rather than being truncated. Judge-side failures (api_error, invalid_judge_output) are excluded from both means: those are our outage, not the model's answer.

task2.note: Task 2 is scored over 4,844 questions - the 4,993 test QA of video_split_60_10_30_v3 minus the 144 the question screening dropped and a net 5 more from the cross-site, re-anchor and re-screen passes. Both Task 2 leakage surfaces are now fixed. The second one closed on 2026-08-14: on four cases Task 2's slides carried captions Task 1's de-leak had already removed - three whole captions naming the panel's own management (a bilateral skin-sparing mastectomy that was performed, two trial regimens with dosing) and a fourth with only its trailing clause cut, which is why counting <image> markers never found it. Task 2's slides are now required to equal Task 1's rather than merely to be de-leaked, which changed the input on 150 of the 4,844 questions. Those 150 answers were regenerated per arm and merged back; the other 4,694 are carried over byte for byte and every record keeps a slide_alignment_source field. The published rubric is task2_judge_v4, adopted 2026-08-15 in place of v3. It differs from v3 in one bullet: the judge is now SHOWN each slide as its image followed by its caption, the two bound together as one piece of evidence, so the judge and a vision candidate look at the same slides. The 1-5 bands, both booleans and the rationale instruction are byte-identical to v3, which is what makes the paired v3/v4 comparison on the same qa_ids interpretable. Under v4 twelve of the thirteen re-judged arms score HIGHER than under v3, by +0.002 to +0.164, and one falls (huatuogpt_3_32b_reasoning, -0.049); showing the judge the slides is not a uniform leniency shift. Every configuration that publishes a Task 2 row is scored under v4. deepseek_v4_flash_api and its reasoning arm were judged in a second batch on 2026-08-15 against the same judge, effort, prompt and schema; they rise +0.030 each. They held ranks 1 and 2 of the fifteen-row board of that day; on today's seventeen rows they are 3rd and 6th, behind qwen3_8_27b_reasoning and deepseek_v4_pro_reasoning. The same unanswered-case rule applies: item_macro_clinical_equivalence_all_responses scores a candidate_format_failure at the rubric floor of 1 and is what the leaderboard reports - 34 of the 62,972 judged records across the thirteen arms. critical_error_rate and unsupported_claim_rate stay on the answered subset, because a question the model never answered contains no critical error and no unsupported claim, and flooring them would report findings that are not in the data. Judge-side failures (api_error, invalid_judge_output) are excluded from both means; there were none.

_notes.derived_judge_inputs: Not generation runs. Each is a published run rewritten so the candidate is its extracted Conclusion alone, which is what task1_judge_v14 scores. input_sha256 and run_config.json pass through unchanged, so a variant still reconciles against the manifest record and registry entry it claims; only raw_response and extracted_final_response are replaced. Produced by model_evaluation/finetune_v1/build_conclusion_only_runs.py; per-run sha256 in conclusion_extraction/conclusion_only_runs_20260811.json. A SECOND derivation kind lives here from 2026-08-12: the *_judgeinput copies of the question-only runs. There only input_sha256 is rewritten, to the full-context manifest record the judge scores against, because the candidate saw the question alone while the judge sees the whole case; the real question-only hash is kept per record in questiononly_input_sha256 and the answer text is byte-identical.
_notes.superseded: Retired by a later artifact of the same kind. policy.source_priority: Later aggregate sources override earlier rows with the same task and model_key.
policy.immutability: Never edit or selectively rerun a published raw response directory.
policy.promotion: A new result becomes active only after catalog update, validation, aggregate rebuild, documentation update, and website tests.
policy.retention: Superseded artifacts remain provenance-only until a separately approved cleanup. Judge batch files - task*.batch.jsonl and their shards - are not retained: they reach 136 GB for one multimodal Task 2 batch and are regenerable from build_config.json, which records the sha256 of every input. What is retained is what cannot be rebuilt: build_config.json, the judge manifest, the per-request outputs and results/. A batch is only reclaimed once its directory has a results/summary.json; an unjudged batch is left alone. Cleanup of 2026-08-15 reclaimed 274 GB on this rule.
policy.task2_withdrawal: Task 2 numbers were withdrawn on 2026-08-08 because its inputs have not been de-leaked. The runs and judge outputs are retained and classified, not deleted; nothing about them was found to be wrong. Republishing requires de-leaking case_summary and slides for Task 2, screening the questions that carry facts the de-leak removes, and re-aggregating over the 4,993-QA test subset.
policy.sampled_decoding_withdrawal: Withdrawn 2026-08-18, the day they were produced. Task 1 at temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 (base and both discussion-table SFT arms, with their judge runs and the BERTScore and ROUGE-L runs built on them) is not protocol-comparable: every other model on the board was decoded greedily, and re-decoding them all is not on the table. Nothing about these runs was found to be wrong and they are retained, not deleted. TWO FINDINGS FROM THEM SURVIVE THE WITHDRAWAL because neither depends on the sampled numbers being publishable. First, the greedy collapse of the discussion-table arms is not caused by the target's register: an arm distilled to third-person prose, first person eliminated on 4,804 of 4,804 rows, collapsed at 96% against the verbatim-speech arm's 97%. Second, the collapse is decoding-dependent, since both arms produce complete output under sampling - so any future greedy result for these arms is a statement about greedy decoding and must say so. Republishing would require the whole board re-decoded under one sampling configuration with a declared seed and n>1 per case.
policy.focused_prompt_study: tumor_board_simulation_focused_multimodal_v1 (sha de8000ec74b531cc) is a STUDY ARTEFACT, not a board prompt, and no result under it is a board number. It is a three-clause edit of tumor_board_simulation_multimodal_v1: 'include every clinically relevant specialty' became 'include only the specialties whose input actually changes the management decision'; a specialist was allowed to appear more than once; and the conclusion spec gained a demand for the specific agent, dose, procedure or interval. The file is retained because two generation runs cite it by path and sha. THE INTERVENTION FAILED AND MUST NOT BE ADOPTED: under the frozen extraction it scores 1.8641 against v1's 2.0815, a net loss of 0.217, because 41 of 184 responses opened a table row for 'Conclusion:' and conclusion_only_v14 then extracted nothing. A post-hoc repair recovers them to 2.1630, but that rule is not part of the pipeline the other twelve models were scored under. On the 143 responses the repair never touched, focused beats v1 by +0.0070 - zero. NONE OF THE THREE FIGURES IS USABLE AS A COMPARATOR. THREE FINDINGS SURVIVE AND ARE WHY THE ARTEFACTS ARE KEPT. First, the cost of requiring a table is not about the table's content: a six-seat generic table and a four-seat specific one score 2.1189 and 2.1259 on the same 143 cases while removing the table entirely scores 2.2517, so seven SFT arms spent themselves varying a dimension the cost does not live in. Second, conclusion_alignment is insensitive to genericness: genetic counseling fell 58%, clinical trial 42%, and specificity rose 3.6x for no change in score, even though the judge's own rationales cite 'unsupported additions' - rationale text must not be used for causal attribution. Third, a termination cue is shared between prompt and target: deleting 'one contribution per specialist' broke the base's format on 22.3% of cases, the same way deleting the speaker-change boundary broke every discussion-table arm.

base_loss_preflight.what: Zero-step base loss on a candidate SFT target: LLaMA-Factory with do_train:false / do_eval:true, base weights untouched, identical tokenisation and label masking, only eval_dataset swapped, each arm measured on its own validation split. About one minute per arm, no training.
base_loss_preflight.why: Six of the eight Task 1 fine-tuning arms were only known to have failed after 90 optimiser steps, a 184-case generation run and a judge run. This number is available before any of that. It measures how UNPREDICTABLE a target is under the untouched base - not how good it is.

measured_20260819.fullturn: OOM on one card - NOT measured; the trainer_log step-5 value 2.423 is used as a stand-in and is labelled as such

base_loss_preflight.does_not_predict_collapse: A gate of the form 'base loss >= 1.8, do not train' was proposed and is REFUTED by conclusiononly, whose base loss is 1.869 - higher than by_role's - and which trained normally and never collapsed. High loss is necessary but not sufficient; collapse also requires a repeatable row structure to supply the absorbing state. A single-block prose target has no row to repeat.
base_loss_preflight.companion_control: A diagnostic dataset that holds every dimension fixed but one turns the number into a decomposition. selftrunc truncates the base model's OWN table to the row count that case has under by_role, leaving prompt, images and conclusion byte-identical: 0.835 -> 1.091 -> 1.768 attributes +0.256 to panel size and +0.677 to cell content.
base_loss_preflight.selftrunc_status: Diagnostic only. Never trained, never generated from, never judged, never a board entry. It exists to be a loss number and nothing else.
base_loss_preflight.what_it_is_not: NOT a go/no-go gate on whether a target is worth training, and NOT a quality score. Both readings were used on 2026-08-19 and both are refuted. (1) conclusiononly's base loss is 1.869 - HIGHER than by_role's 1.768 - and it trained normally, never collapsed, and scored +0.038. (2) The reference conclusion itself, the object the judge scores against, has a base loss of 1.990, higher than by_role's table at 1.744: the ground truth is less predictable than the target being judged against it. A good clinical discussion SHOULD be unpredictable from the case summary and slides - that is what makes it worth supervising. A LOW number is the bad sign: selftable's table scores 0.501 precisely because the base already writes it, which is why that arm taught nothing and returned +0.0109 (n.s.).
base_loss_preflight.the_one_valid_use: Paired comparison between targets that share a structure, with every other dimension held fixed by a companion diagnostic dataset. selftable 0.835 -> selftrunc 1.091 -> by_role 1.768 attributes +0.256 to panel size and +0.677 to cell content, and that decomposition is sound because selftrunc changes exactly one thing. Comparing across structures - a two-row table against a twelve-row one, a table against a bare conclusion - reads unpredictability as quality and is wrong.
base_loss_preflight.what_actually_predicts_collapse: Two conditions together, not one. High base loss says the target is unlike what the model writes - necessary, not sufficient. Collapse also needs a REPEATABLE ROW STRUCTURE to supply the absorbing state. conclusiononly emits one block of prose with no row to repeat and cannot loop however high its loss. by_role's rows are role-unique, so copying a row means copying a role name that no training example shows - and it did not collapse.
base_loss_preflight.surface_axis_is_capped: Role labels are 2.1% of the target's tokens (median 8 of 354), so casing, row order and header wording can move this number by at most about 2% however they are set. Title Case buys -0.015 and a fixed clinical order costs +0.005. Do not spend measurement time on that axis again.
